Subject: Pilot economics sprint check-in

Emma — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps from today's discovery so we have alignment heading into the pilot week:

Key takeaways
- Workload: real-time product search reranking + short summaries for checkout flows. Median prompt ~220 tokens, 95th ~1200 tokens.
- Expected traffic (pilot): 25k–40k requests/day; estimated token burn: 6M–10M tokens/day (gross).
- Success criteria: 90% of queries under 300ms p95 and <5% regression in quality vs current model baseline.

Pricing / budget signals you shared
- Target spend range for pilot: $30k–$60k/month (includes safety buffer).
- Target unit economics your finance team prefers: goal ~ $150–$220 per 1M tokens during pilot evaluation.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) We (Redwood) to propose a short unit-econ table and a one-off credit to cover initial burn for 2 weeks.
2) You to confirm exact daily peak windows so we can size autoscaling and provide latency SLOs.
3) If pilot numbers hold, we’ll draft a one-page addendum (credits + usage bands) for signature.

Attachments
- I attached a quick spreadsheet with a conservative + aggressive burn projection (BC-Pilot-Usage-Projections.xlsx).

If anything above is off, call it out — otherwise I’ll turn the econ numbers into a concrete credit proposal tomorrow and route for approval.

Thanks,
Ben Carter | Senior Account Executive

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 6M–10M/day estimate is our best guess based on full catalog rush windows; expect most of the traffic in a 4-hour evening window (ET).
- Finance confirmed the pilot budget envelope is $40k–$55k/month if the unit econ lands near $160/1M tokens. If we can get an effective rate near $150/1M for the pilot that materially improves our odds.
- We would need at least a 30% credit buffer to get through the first 10 business days — execs want to avoid any service interruption during Black Friday carryover testing next month.

Can you confirm what a 30% credit buffer would look like in dollars for the first two weeks (rough estimate is fine) and whether Redwood can approve an initial top-up without a PO in place? Also curious if there’s a preferred cadence to switch to committed capacity if we see steady usage.

—Emma

Emma — thanks, that's helpful. Quick math and proposal: 

Conservative pilot scenario (baseline)
- 6M tokens/day -> ~180M tokens/month. At target $160/1M tokens -> $28,800/month.
Aggressive scenario
- 10M tokens/day -> ~300M tokens/month -> $48,000/month at $160/1M.

30% credit buffer calculation
- If we target the conservative monthly spend ($28.8k), a 30% buffer = ~$8.6k. If we target the aggressive monthly spend ($48k), 30% = ~$14.4k. For the first two weeks (50% of month) those dollar amounts scale to ~ $4.3k–$7.2k.

What Redwood can offer now
- I’ll route a one-time pilot credit in the $5k–$15k range depending on how aggressive you want to be. We commonly do an initial credit + a conditional top-up if usage trends above the conservative band.
- We can approve an initial top-up without a PO (internal approvals required for larger amounts). Anything over $10k needs sign-off from finance which I can start now.
- If usage stabilizes above ~200M tokens/month, we recommend switching to Reserved (Dedicated) lanes for predictable throughput and a discounted unit rate — we can model committed bands and show savings.

Proposed next steps
1) Emma: confirm which buffer target you prefer (conservative/aggressive) and whether a one-time $10k credit meets your execs' risk tolerance.
2) Redwood: I'll prepare a credit addendum (one-page) + a short committed-capacity sketch by EOD tomorrow for internal sign-off.
3) Ops: Monica will coordinate a short runbook for Black Friday window scaling — cc'ing her here.

Attachment: BrightCart_Credit_Addendum.pdf (draft) — includes terms for credit expiration and safety net rules.

Ben

- If BrightCart opts for the aggressive buffer (~$14k+), I will need a short note from your finance team authorizing that upper range so we have cost accountability.
- I'll work with Billing to mark the credit and set tracking tags to ensure we can report burn daily. Laura, can you confirm the DocuSign link and expiration window (I suggest 45 days).
